steps: Initiator records local state and sends marker messages.
A process records state when it sees its first marker.
It records messages on other channels until their markers arrive.
Combined process and channel records form a consistent global cut.

lesson.scenario: Two account processes use Chandy-Lamport markers to capture a consistent cut including an in-transit payment.
connections: Report A state and BA channel log
Report B state and AB channel log

steps.title: Record the initiator state
steps.narration: A snapshots local balance=100 before any later receive, starts recording incoming channel B->A, and places marker M1 after all earlier A->B messages.
action: Record balance 100 then send marker M1

processB.detail: No work accepted in this phase

channelAB.detail: marker M1 after prior messages; FIFO=true

channelBA.detail: A records messages until marker M1

steps.outcome: A fixes its side of the cut and opens one channel recording.
steps.invariant: A process records local state before sending markers, FIFO channels order each marker after earlier application messages, incoming messages are recorded from local snapshot until that channel marker, and the collected cut contains no receive whose send is absent.

steps.title: Send before observing the marker
steps.narration: Before M1 reaches B, B changes live balance 80->70 and sends p77 amount=10 on B->A.
action: Debit 10 and send payment p77 to A

channelAB.detail: M1 not yet delivered to B

steps.outcome: The payment crosses the snapshot cut in transit.
steps.invariant: A process records local state before sending markers, FIFO channels order each marker after earlier application messages, incoming messages are recorded from local snapshot until that channel marker, and the collected cut contains no receive whose send is absent.

steps.title: Record the in-transit message
steps.narration: A applies p77 to live balance 110 but appends p77 to the snapshot state of channel B->A because its marker has not arrived.
action: Deliver p77 while A records channel

channelAB.detail: M1 not yet delivered to B

steps.outcome: The cut keeps A local state at 100 and accounts for the transferred 10 in the channel.
steps.invariant: A process records local state before sending markers, FIFO channels order each marker after earlier application messages, incoming messages are recorded from local snapshot until that channel marker, and the collected cut contains no receive whose send is absent.

steps.title: Record the first-marker receiver
steps.narration: On its first marker, B records local balance=70, records A->B channel empty, and sends M1 on B->A after its earlier p77 due to FIFO ordering.
steps.outcome: B fixes its local cut and closes one incoming channel immediately.
steps.invariant: A process records local state before sending markers, FIFO channels order each marker after earlier application messages, incoming messages are recorded from local snapshot until that channel marker, and the collected cut contains no receive whose send is absent.

steps.title: Close and validate the consistent cut
steps.narration: A stops recording B->A and reports channel state {p77}; the collector totals A=100+B=70+inTransit=10, preserving the original 180.
steps.outcome: The snapshot contains no receive without its send and captures the in-flight transfer exactly once.
steps.invariant: A process records local state before sending markers, FIFO channels order each marker after earlier application messages, incoming messages are recorded from local snapshot until that channel marker, and the collected cut contains no receive whose send is absent.

production.scenario: A Flink fraud feature pipeline checkpoints operator state so card-authorization scoring can resume without corrupting model inputs.
components: global card auth events feeding realtime fraud features and models
service boundary that validates schemas and injects jobs into the streaming topology
control-plane service that captures a consistent cut across pipeline operators and offsets
durable authority in object storage for checkpoint manifests, offsets, and operator state files
serves committed features to online scoring only after checkpoint-safe processing
control path that triggers savepoints, rollback, and region recovery after pipeline faults
observability path for checkpoint duration, restore success, and state growth
flows: Authorization events cross into the streaming domain through the schema-enforcing pipeline boundary.
The gateway and runtime trigger the snapshot coordinator to inject a new checkpoint across the topology.
Operator state, offsets, and manifests are written into the authoritative checkpoint store as one recoverable cut.
The serving layer exposes only feature materializations backed by the durable checkpoint lineage.
Recovery control asks the snapshot coordinator to roll back or promote a savepoint after faults.
The checkpoint store returns the exact state files and offsets needed for deterministic restore.
Dashboards report checkpoint lag, state bloat, and restore time against fraud SLOs.
